articles.title: Haris Rauf punished for on-field confrontation during Pakistan's  win over England
articles.summary: Pakistan fast bowler Haris Rauf has been fined 20 per cent of his match fee and received a demerit point for his on-field behaviour during Sunday's ODI
articles.body: Pakistan fast bowler Haris Rauf has been fined 20 per cent of his match fee and received a demerit point for his on-field behaviour during Sunday's ODI against England in Lahore. The visitors were also penalised after failing to maintain the required over-rate.The International Cricket Council (ICC) confirmed that Rauf breached Article 2.2 of its Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which covers conduct contrary to the spirit of the game. He received an official reprimand, taking his tally to five demerit points following his third offence within a 24-month period.The incident occurred towards the end of Pakistan's innings, after the 46th over, when Rauf was at the non-striker's end. The pacer appealed for a wide before getting into an argument with England all-rounder Will Jacks.Rauf raised his bat during the exchange and continued the argument despite being warned by umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid. He then brushed past the umpire while moving towards Jacks.England were handed a separate penalty, with their players fined 15 per cent of their match fees for maintaining an over-rate three overs below the required level, even after time allowances were taken into account.The sanction was imposed under Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct, which provides for a five per cent fine on players' match fees for every over a team falls short of the minimum over-rate requirement.Both Rauf and England captain Harry Brook accepted the charges and the penalties proposed by Jeff Crowe of the Emirates ICC Elite Panel of Match Referees. As a result, neither case required a formal hearing.The charges against the two teams were brought by on-field umpires Rashid Riaz and Sharfuddoula, third umpire Wayne Knights and fourth umpire Nassir Hussain.The disciplinary action followed a dramatic contest in which Pakistan secured a one-wicket victory while chasing England's total. Shadab Khan played a decisive role with an unbeaten century to keep Pakistan in the hunt during the closing stages.Shadab and Rauf then stitched together an unbroken 89-run partnership for the final wicket to take Pakistan over the line with 17 balls remaining.The victory also booked Pakistan's place in the ODI tri-series final, where they are scheduled to face Sri Lanka on October 31.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: James Anderson set to continue playing career in Italy with Napoli ‌Knights in the Italia T10 league
articles.summary: James Anderson is now set to captain and co-own the Napoli ‌Knights, one of six teams in the Italia T10 league; after international retirement, England great Anderson continued playing for Lancashire and captained the county this year but Lancashire elected not to renew his contract
articles.body:
He will captain and co-own the Napoli ‌Knights, one of six teams in the Italia T10 league as the 44-year-old extends his career after being released by Lancashire, his club of 25 years.

Anderson, who played more than 400 times for England across all formats and took nearly 1,000 wickets, is a big name to join the format.

The Italia T10 league is a 10-over-a-side ​competition, which takes place over 12 days at the Roma Cricket Ground from November 18.

It was created by Nadeem Shahid, a former professional cricketer, and Aamir Akhtar, who helped set up the Everest ​Premier League in his native Nepal.

High-profile players such as Chris Gayle, Shaun Marsh and Dawid Malan ‌will also feature, joined by members of the Italian national side who impressed earlier this year when they narrowly lost to England at the T20 World Cup.

"The potential for cricket in ⁠Italy made it a big draw," Shahid told Reuters. "One of the things ‌that made it attractive is the Italian Olympic Committee beginning to take it seriously after it became an Olympic sport."

He noted: "Tickets will be free for all the matches, and there will be coaching clinics on the sidelines."

Anderson's company, Activate Sport & Leisure, will be involved in ‌some of those clinics, as Italy looks to develop homegrown talent capable of competing at Olympic level by the time of the 2032 Games in Brisbane.

"Of course, we want Napoli Knights to be competitive and challenge for the title, but we also want to contribute to something that continues to grow well beyond the tournament itself," Anderson said.

articles.title: Ravindra Jadeja loses No. 1 Test all-rounder crown after four years; Abhishek Sharma dethrones Kishan to top T20I batting rankings
articles.summary: Abhishek Sharma has reclaimed the No.
articles.body: Abhishek Sharma has reclaimed the No. 1 spot in the ICC T20I batting rankings, overtaking India teammate Ishan Kishan, while South Africa all-rounder Marco Jansen has become the top-ranked Test bowler and Test all-rounder for the first time in his career.Jansen's rise to the top in two categories follows his performance in South Africa's comprehensive victory over Australia in the second Test in Gqeberha. The left-arm pacer scored 85 runs with the bat and took a match-turning five-wicket haul in Australia's first innings.The performance helped Jansen improve his position across all three Test ranking categories. The 26-year-old climbed 13 places to 56th among Test batters, moved up five spots to overtake Mitchell Starc as the No. 1 Test bowler and rose one place to displace India's Ravindra Jadeja as the top-ranked Test all-rounder.Jadeja had held the No. 1 position among Test all-rounders for more than four years. Jansen's rise to the top comes after former South Africa great Dale Steyn recently described him as 'the best cricketer in the world'.Abhishek's return to the top of the T20I batting rankings came after his century against New Zealand in the third match of their series in Wellington on Tuesday.The left-hander reached his hundred in just 35 balls and finished with 113 off 38 deliveries as India registered a six-wicket victory to seal the series. His innings helped him overtake Kishan and reclaim the No. 1 position among T20I batters.Kishan had moved to the top of the rankings in July this year after a series of good performances in Ireland. Abhishek had first reached the No. 1 spot in July 2025, when he overtook Australia's Travis Head.Several other players also moved up in the latest ICC rankings. South Africa captain Temba Bavuma climbed four places to second among Test batters after being named Player of the Match for his performance against Australia in the second Test.India captain Shubman Gill remains the top-ranked ODI batter, with Virat Kohli in third place and Rohit Sharma at No. 4.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'It's not easy to let go of  batting position': Abhishek Sharma hails Sanju Samson's sacrifice for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: In a team where individual milestones often command the spotlight, Sanju Samson chose to put the team ahead of himself.
articles.body: In a team where individual milestones often command the spotlight, Sanju Samson chose to put the team ahead of himself. Fresh off a match-winning 61, the India wicketkeeper-batter gave up his opening slot to teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi in the third T20I against New Zealand, a selfless call that earned him rich praise from opening partner Abhishek Sharma after India's six-wicket win.Abhishek led India's charge with a breathtaking 38-ball 113, while Sooryavanshi made the most of his promotion with a blistering 45 off just 19 deliveries. The duo stitched together a mammoth 133-run partnership in seven overs, putting India firmly in control of the chase.Sooryavanshi was promoted to open after batting at No. 3 in the previous match. The teenager had initially come into the side following Ishan Kishan's groin injury, but it was Samson's decision to vacate his opening position that allowed the youngster to move up the order.Samson had himself enjoyed a productive outing in the second T20I, winning the Player of the Match award for his 61. Despite that performance, he stepped aside to give Sooryavanshi an opportunity at the top, earning appreciation from his opening partner."The way Sanju bhai batted in the last game, it is not easy to let go of one's familiar batting position. That showed his character, someone's going at his position. We can see in the team that everyone is selfless, everyone is happy for everyone, which is the hallmark of a great team," Abhishek told Sooryavanshi in a conversation facilitated by BCCI.TV.Abhishek, Sooryavanshi power India to emphatic winIndia defeated New Zealand by six wickets in the third T20I on Tuesday to take an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series.Batting first, New Zealand posted 198/3, with Daryl Mitchell top-scoring with an unbeaten 89 off 52 balls. Finn Allen contributed 40, while India's bowlers pulled things back towards the end to keep the hosts below 200.In reply, Abhishek Sharma produced a breathtaking performance, smashing 113 off just 38 balls, including nine fours and 11 sixes. He reached his century in 35 deliveries and shared a 133-run opening partnership with 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who scored 45 off 19 balls.India raced to 118 without loss in the Powerplay before completing the chase in 13.2 overs, with 40 balls remaining. The emphatic victory secured the series for India with two matches to spare.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Not a concern': 118 runs in four innings, no fifty in tri-series but Babar Azam still has Pakistan's backing
articles.summary: Pakistan batting coach Mike Smith has backed Babar Azam despite the batter's recent struggles to score big, saying there is no reason to worry as Pakistan
articles.body: Pakistan batting coach Mike Smith has backed Babar Azam despite the batter's recent struggles to score big, saying there is no reason to worry as Pakistan prepare to face Sri Lanka in the tri-series final on Saturday.Pakistan suffered their first defeat of the series on Tuesday, losing to Sri Lanka by eight wickets in Lahore. Babar top-scored for Pakistan with 29, but the team's batting lineup collapsed as they were bowled out for just 110.Babar has scored 118 runs in four innings in the tri-series but is yet to register a half-century. Although the former Pakistan captain has managed to get starts in each innings, he has been unable to turn them into bigger scores.Smith, however, is not concerned about Babar's form. He pointed to Pakistan's unbeaten run before Tuesday's defeat as a sign of the team's overall performance."It is definitely not a cause for concern," Smith said as per the ICC website."The hardest part of batting in cricket is getting established at the crease, and Babar is doing that effortlessly. Had he converted one of those solid starts into a substantial century, this would not even be a topic of discussion. That is the nature of elite international sport—you cannot deliver a peak performance every single time. Those who truly understand the game can see how well he is striking the ball. We have zero doubt that a big score is imminent, and when it comes, it will be magnificent to watch," he added.Pakistan's batting collapse on Tuesday was led by Sri Lanka pacer Dilshan Madushanka, who took five wickets. The left-arm bowler troubled the hosts with the new ball and returned later in the innings to help bowl them out for 110. Sri Lanka then completed the chase comfortably.Smith admitted that the defeat was not the ideal preparation for the final but said it would not affect Pakistan's chances of winning the title."That defeat will have no bearing whatsoever on the final," Smith said."In a tri-series of this caliber against quality opposition, very few teams remain undefeated throughout. A setback at some point is expected. Losing the game leading into the final changes nothing. Ultimately, a final comes down to whichever team handles the pressure best on the day and executes under strain to lift the trophy," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Baap ka, dada ka, bhai ka': Wasseypur dialogue fires up Vaishnavi Sharma as she takes 'sabka badla' against Zimbabwe
articles.summary: India wicketkeeper Yastika Bhatia found a unique way to motivate left-arm spinner Vaishnavi Sharma during the third women's ODI against Zimbabwe in
articles.body: India wicketkeeper Yastika Bhatia found a unique way to motivate left-arm spinner Vaishnavi Sharma during the third women's ODI against Zimbabwe in Vadodara on Wednesday, borrowing a famous dialogue from the Hindi film Gangs of Wasseypur 2.As Vaishnavi troubled the Zimbabwe batters, Yastika was heard saying from behind the stumps: "Vaishu (Vaishnavi) sabka badla lena hai. Baap ka, dada ka, bhai ka,"The line is a reference to a famous dialogue delivered by Nawazuddin Siddiqui's character Faizal in Gangs of Wasseypur 2: "Baap ka, dada ka, bhai ka, sabka badla lega re tera Faizal." In the film, Faizal says it to signal that he will avenge the murders of his father, grandfather and brother by his family's rivals.Vaishnavi responded with a five-wicket haul as India bowled Zimbabwe out for 131 in the third ODI. The left-arm spinner finished with figures of five for 39 in 10 overs, completing her maiden five-wicket haul in ODIs with the final ball of her spell.The 20-year-old had taken four wickets in the second ODI at the same venue.Vaishnavi repeatedly tossed the ball up and tempted the Zimbabwe batters into playing their shots, leading to their collapse. Opener Modester Mupachikwa was the visitors' top scorer with 37 off 48 balls.Zimbabwe's problems began early, with a series of soft dismissals putting the team under pressure. The visitors had struggled with the bat throughout their white-ball tour of India.Pacer Sayali Satghare struck in her first over, with opener Loryn Phiri edging the ball faintly down the leg side. Number three Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano was the next to fall after cutting a regulation delivery from Shafali Verma straight to the fielder at point.Vaishnavi then took control of the innings. She first dismissed Beloved Biza before getting the better of Mupachikwa, who had been in good form. Anticipating that the opener would step out of her crease, Vaishnavi bowled a wide, flighted delivery. Mupachikwa was stumped by Yastika.Vaishnavi claimed her fifth and final wicket off the last ball of her spell. Nyasha Gwanzura attempted a slog sweep, but the ball ricocheted off her pads and hit the stumps.While Vaishnavi led the bowling effort, Kranti Gaud and Satghare picked up two wickets each.With the series already secured, India made three changes to their playing XI for the third ODI, bringing in Harleen Deol, Yastika and Gaud. Gaud had been rested for the second ODI.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Best player I’ve ever played with': Aaron Finch reveals what sets Steve Smith apart from David Warner and other batters
articles.summary: Former Australia white-ball captain Aaron Finch believes Steve Smith stands in a league of his own, describing the star batter as the best player he has
articles.body: Former Australia white-ball captain Aaron Finch believes Steve Smith stands in a league of his own, describing the star batter as the best player he has shared a dressing room with. From being a leg-spinner batting at No. 8 to becoming one of the most accomplished batters of his generation, Smith’s remarkable rise has been driven by a rare combination of natural talent, relentless hard work and an unwavering belief in his own methods, according to Finch.Smith, who was once viewed as a potential successor to legendary leg-spinner Shane Warne, has gone on to establish himself as one of Australia's greatest modern-day batters. He has occupied the No. 1 spot in the ICC Test batting rankings and captained Australia across formats, transforming his game through years of refinement and an unconventional approach that has often set him apart from his contemporaries.Speaking on Cricinfo's show, Finch reflected on Smith's evolution, his distinctive batting technique and the mental strength that has helped him thrive at the highest level.‘He turned into this absolute gun of a batter’Finch recalled how Smith initially entered Australian cricket as a bowling all-rounder, with his batting playing a secondary role. However, a significant change in his approach eventually unlocked his potential and turned him into one of the most formidable run-scorers in world cricket.“Steve Smith went from being touted as Shane Warne’s replacement, starting at eight in the batting order, bowling a few overs of leg spin, getting the odd runs as the finisher. Then something changed overnight. He turned into this absolute gun of a batter that took the world by storm,” Finch said.“He was always a handsy player with big movements, moving his feet a lot. Then he simplified that and everything clicked,” Finch added.Smith's ability to establish himself in the middle order and subsequently make the No. 4 position his own further demonstrated his adaptability. For Finch, however, the defining feature of Smith's batting has been his willingness to trust his instincts, regardless of how unconventional his methods might appear.“The ability to go from number six and five for so long and then slip into number four in the batting order was extraordinary. He’s the best player I’ve ever played with by a mile. He says, I’m doing it this way; I don’t care what it looks like to the outside world. This is what will make me most successful,” Finch said.“That is a superpower. To see what he does when others can’t, you can’t explain why players like me or David Warner couldn’t do it, but he could. It’s a natural gift, but also hard work, the hours he’s put in. It’s extraordinary.”How stepping away from captaincy helped SmithSmith's career also endured a major setback following Australia's ball-tampering scandal in Cape Town in 2018. The incident resulted in a 12-month ban from international and domestic cricket under Cricket Australia's sanctions, alongside a two-year prohibition on holding a leadership position.He eventually returned to the international setup and later became vice-captain to current Test skipper Pat Cummins. Finch believes the absence of captaincy responsibilities after the scandal may have helped Smith rediscover his focus as a batter.According to Finch, the demands of leadership had often required Smith to divide his attention between his own preparation and the needs of the wider team. Being relieved of those responsibilities allowed him to concentrate more fully on his individual game.“After the 2018 incident, coming back into the international setup, Steve Smith was more relaxed as a player because he didn’t have the captaincy for obvious reasons. As captain, so much of your time goes into things away from your own game,” Finch said.He explained that Smith's meticulous preparation could also become mentally demanding when combined with the responsibility of managing a team.“And then getting the amount of work he wanted done put extra pressure on him mentally, because you need to get this much work done to feel ready to go, but you’ve still got to worry about everybody else,” he added.Finch also admitted that captaining Australia with Smith in the team initially proved challenging for him. Having previously played under Smith, he held the batter's tactical judgement in high regard and sometimes found himself questioning his own decisions.“I found it really difficult to captain with him in the side at the start, because I’d played under him for quite a bit of time and tactically, I thought he was an outstanding captain. So, I found myself at times being like, is this the right move? What would Smith think?”However, Smith eventually encouraged Finch to trust his own judgement rather than seek constant reassurance.“And then one day he just said, why do you keep asking me? Just make your own decision,” Finch recalled.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Marnus Labuschagne extended his unwanted record on Wednesday, going 48 Test innings without a century as Australia reached 90/2 at lunch on Day 2 of the
articles.body: Marnus Labuschagne extended his unwanted record on Wednesday, going 48 Test innings without a century as Australia reached 90/2 at lunch on Day 2 of the decisive third Test against South Africa at Newlands.His ongoing drought is now the longest among Australian top-four batters, with his last Test hundred coming in July 2023.Australia reached 90 for two at lunch on Day 2 of the decisive third Test against South Africa on Wednesday, after spinner Simon Harmer took two wickets in his first over.Australia are still 239 runs behind South Africa’s first-innings total of 329, with eight wickets remaining.Matt Renshaw remained unbeaten on 27, while Cameron Green was on 17 at the break. The pair will look to rebuild Australia’s innings in the afternoon session.Harmer strikes, Labuschagne strugglesAustralia made a steady start, reaching the first drinks break without losing a wicket. Renshaw and Travis Head added 58 runs for the opening stand before Harmer changed the game with two quick strikes.Head was bowled for 41 after chopping the ball onto his stumps while playing off the back foot. Five balls later, Marnus Labuschagne was caught at slip by Aiden Markram for a duck, leaving Australia struggling at 58-2.Labuschagne’s dismissal extended his disappointing run in Test cricket. He has now gone 48 innings without a century, having last scored a hundred in July 2023. This is the longest century drought for an Australian batter in the top four.Renshaw, who was promoted to open after Nic Maddinson was dropped following poor performances in the first two Tests, showed patience at the crease. He last opened in Test cricket in 2018, also against South Africa in Johannesburg. Renshaw and Green added 32 runs in nine overs to steady Australia before lunch.Series decider could decide World No. 1The three-match series is level at 1-1, making the final Test crucial for both teams. Australia won the opening match in Durban by 214 runs, but South Africa bounced back in Gqeberha with an innings-and-31-run victory.The winner of the Newlands Test will claim the top spot in the Test world rankings, currently held by Australia. With South Africa having posted 329 in their first innings, Australia face an important challenge in the remaining sessions.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Australia reach 330-4 on day two of third Test decider, with Josh Inglis (85 not out), Alex Carey (51 not out) digging in to put visitors in strong position vs South Africa at Newlands; South Africa 329 all out on day one; watch day three live on Thursday from 8am on Sky Sports+
articles.body:
Australia are one run ahead of South ​Africa's score of 329 and in control of the match as they now look to build a commanding lead.

Inglis, who ​came into the side for the injured Steve Smith, ‌shared an unbeaten 145-run partnership with Alex Carey (51 not out) for the fifth wicket.

South Africa ​toiled in the field as all Australian batters except Marnus Labuschagne (0) got in and scored runs.

The Newlands wicket is traditionally best for batting on ​days two and three and so it proved as ⁠there was little seam or swing ⁠for the home side's pace attack.

Matt Renshaw and Travis Head (41) added 58 for the first wicket before spinner ‌Simon Harmer (2-84) removed the latter with his first ball of the match.

Head chopped the ball on to his stumps playing off the back foot, an ‌all too familiar mode of dismissal for him in recent times.

Labuschagne's poor run in Tests continued when he fell for a duck, caught by Aiden Markram at slip off Harmer.

Renshaw and Cameron Green added 126 for the third ⁠wicket before they also fell in quick succession, this ​time to fast bowler Marco Jansen (2-37).

Renshaw was caught by ​wicketkeeper Ryan Rickelton and Green edged to Harmer at slip.

Another ​substantial partnership from Inglis and Carey, however, means the momentum remains ⁠with Australia as South Africa failed to apply scoreboard pressure or create many wicket-taking opportunities.

The series is level at 1-1 after Australia won the first Test ⁠by 214 runs in Durban and South ​Africa responded with a victory by an innings and 31 runs ​in Gqeberha.

The team who win the match will occupy the number one position in the Test world rankings, which ‌is currently held by Australia.

articles.summary: India completed a 3-0 sweep of the women’s ODI series against Zimbabwe after registering a convincing eight-wicket victory in the third match on Wednesday.
articles.body: India completed a 3-0 sweep of the women’s ODI series against Zimbabwe after registering a convincing eight-wicket victory in the third match on Wednesday.Young left-arm spinner Vaishnavi Sharma starred with five wickets, while Pratika Rawal and Shafali Verma scored unbeaten half-centuries to help India chase the target of 132 in just 17 overs.Playing only her third ODI, the 20-year-old Vaishnavi delivered an impressive performance, taking five wickets for 39 runs in her 10 overs. She had also picked up four wickets in the second ODI, showing her growing impact at the international level.Vaishnavi troubled the Zimbabwe batters with her flight and variations, forcing them into mistakes. Zimbabwe were bowled out for 131 in 39.5 overs, with opener Modester Mupachikwa top-scoring with 37 off 48 balls.India’s fast bowlers also contributed to the visitors’ collapse. Sayali Satghare struck in her first over to dismiss opener Loryn Phiri, while Shafali Verma removed Chipo Mugeri-Tiripano.Vaishnavi then took control, dismissing key batters, including Mupachikwa, who was stumped after stepping out of her crease. Kranti Gaud and Satghare picked up two wickets each to support the spinner.Pratika and Shafali finish the chaseIndia’s chase suffered an early setback when Yastika Bhatia was caught at mid-on off the first ball she faced. However, Pratika kept the innings steady and continued her strong run in the series after scoring 100 and 61 in the first two matches.Batting at number three, Pratika struck an unbeaten 59 off 56 balls, recording her 10th ODI half-century in her 30th match. Shafali joined her and accelerated the scoring with an aggressive display, smashing an unbeaten 51 off just 26 deliveries.The pair ensured India reached the target comfortably without losing another wicket.India had also won the preceding T20 series 3-0, completing a clean sweep across both formats. The ODI series was the first bilateral women’s cricket series between India and Zimbabwe, giving the visitors valuable experience against a top international side. articles.title: Lamar Jackson replies to fan's TikTok criticizing Ravens over his injury
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson's latest injury update also included a back-and-forth with NFL insider Ian Rapoport. Here's the latest on the ailing Ravens QB.
articles.body:
One thing is for certain when it comes to the Baltimore Ravens ' starting quarterback for Week 8: he'll be a Pro Bowler.

Starting quarterback Lamar Jackson has missed exactly half of his team's playing time through seven weeks. Jackson sustained a high ankle sprain at the end of the first half of the Ravens ' Week 4 win over the Tennessee Titans . Since then, 2022 Pro Bowler Tyler "Snoop" Huntley has filled in for the starter for three and a half games.

Jackson returned to practice in a limited capacity ahead of Week 7 after the Ravens held him out for every practice in Weeks 5 and 6. The quarterback told reporters on Friday, Oct. 23, that he was "headed in the right direction" but needed to feel like himself before he would play. Ultimately, he missed last week's clash with the Cincinnati Bengals .

After dropping the matchup with Cincinnati, the Ravens fell to last place in the AFC North. Next up is another tough test within their conference: playing at the Buffalo Bills in Week 8 on Sunday, Nov. 1.

Here's what to know about Jackson's outlook for Baltimore's next game:

Cheerleaders, celebrities, fans and mascots at NFL games during 2026 season

NFL Media and ESPN insider Ian Rapoport reported on Tuesday, Oct. 27, that Jackson will play in Week 8.

"I expect, based on the people I've spoken with, that Lamar Jackson will play this week. He'll be on the field this week against the Buffalo Bills," Rapoport said. "He is believed to be as close to 100% as he has been, and the Ravens do expect him to play."

Rapoport also addressed how his previous reporting became part of the storyline in Jackson's recovery. When asked by a reporter on Oct. 23 if he had suffered a deltoid sprain, the quarterback said he was told it was a high ankle sprain and asked who reported it. When Jackson found out it was a report from Rapoport, he had a quip ready.

"Ian Rapoport said that? He part of the training staff?" Jackson said before shaking his head. "So we can't go off Ian Rapoport. He's just reporting. Somebody probably told him that too though, so can't blame him."

The insider joked on Oct. 27 that "the idiots at Bleacher Report" twisted Jackson's comments into calling out Rapoport, but he took it as a light-hearted jab.

"Watch it with a normal brain. He was funny," Rapoport said. "I had said it was not a typical high ankle sprain – it was not. They told him it's a high ankle sprain because it's not low, it's fine."

Lamar Jackson responds to fan video calling out Ravens

A TikTok user called "mrpowell78" criticized the Ravens for misrepresenting the nature of Jackson's injuries whenever he gets hurt in a video he posted on Oct. 27.

"Every time he gets hurt, they don't explain the severity of his injury. They always say, 'Oh, he's day-to-day.' Or 'He shouldn't be out too long.' 'He should be back any time.' He had a high ankle sprain! If you know anything about a high ankle sprain, that's normally like a four- to six-week injury, minimum."

According to Cleveland Clinic , a high ankle sprain may take six to eight weeks to recover from, with a longer recovery time possible for athletes.

The TikTok video continues with mrpowell78 asserting that Jackson has gotten more criticism for his injury than Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown, who suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1. He also said Jackson can't "play hurt" the way other quarterbacks might be able to.

"Other quarterbacks not like my quarterback! My quarterback is a Lamborghini. Your quarterback is a Chevy Cobalt. They not the same," mrpowell78 said.

Jackson commented on the video shortly after it was posted.

"[People] like you are the ones I play so hard for," the Ravens' quarterback wrote.

Huntley is 1-2 in his three starts this season filling in for Jackson. The 2026 season is the second year in his third stint in Baltimore. It's his seventh overall year with the Ravens, all of which he's spent as a backup or practice squad quarterback for the Ravens.

Fagnano signed with the Ravens as an undrafted free agent in April. The rookie has not yet appeared in a game for Baltimore during the regular season.

articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Aneeshwar Gautam grinds his way to maiden ton; Karnataka eye innings win
articles.summary: MYSURU: In 2022, months after being part of India’s U-19 World Cup-winning team, Aneeshwar Gautam received his maiden Ranji Trophy call-up.
articles.body: MYSURU: In 2022, months after being part of India’s U-19 World Cup-winning team, Aneeshwar Gautam received his maiden Ranji Trophy call-up. Though he did not make his Karnataka senior-team debut then, the stint gave him a taste of the dressing-room environment.What followed was a few years of rebuilding after a slump in form, captaining the state U-23 side and making his mark as an all-rounder in league cricket and the KSCA Maharaja Trophy T20 tournament.The hard yards earned him another call-up this season. With several regular batters away on India duty, Aneeshwar made his Karnataka debut against Saurashtra last week. Batting lower down the order, he admitted that nerves got the better of him, and he managed just seven runs across two innings.On Wednesday, against Tripura, the 23-year-old found his rhythm. After 200 deliveries and 298 minutes at the crease, he looked up at the sky, removed his helmet and raised his bat. There was little exuberance after he flicked a Parvez Sultan delivery to fine leg for a single to bring up his maiden first-class century. The understated celebration mirrored his innings — unhurried and built on patience, with a blend of old-world grace and modern strokeplay.At the SDNRW Ground here, it was a day for Karnataka’s rookies to make their presence felt. Manvanth Kumar continued to impress with an entertaining 51 (75b, 6x4, 2x6), while No. 10 Ritesh Bhatkal, who has showcased his batting prowess in KSCA league cricket, produced a stroke-filled unbeaten 74 off 100 balls (11x4, 1x6).Their contributions helped Karnataka reach 490/9 in 144 overs before declaring, stretching their lead to 296. Needing a win to strengthen their push for a knockout berth, Karnataka made an encouraging start with the ball, but Tripura’s batters offered resistance and reached 98/3 in 38 overs. On a flat track, leg-spinner Shreyas Gopal claimed 3/25 to leave the visitors still trailing by 198 runs and his team in a position of command.Resuming the penultimate day at 33, Aneeshwar was intent on grinding it out. Patience was his greatest asset, and Karnataka needed plenty of it after slipping to seven down. With the hosts keen to build a substantial cushion and avoid batting again, the left-hander joined hands with Manvanth to add 85 runs for the eighth wicket.Having spent the past couple of years together in the state U-23 setup and franchise cricket, the duo complemented each other well, rotating the strike while Manvanth took the more aggressive approach.Aneeshwar needed 110 balls to reach his half-century, while Manvanth got there in 71, marking the milestone with a lofted six over midwicket. Manvanth’s entertaining knock ended when Sandip Sarkar (3/147) trapped him in front, but Ritesh took over with an innings that featured 11 fours and a solitary six.At the other end, Aneeshwar tightened up further after crossing 70, and boundaries dried up. The next 30 runs took him another 70 deliveries, with 56 singles accounting for much of his eventual century. His 107-run partnership with Ritesh ended soon after he reached his milestone, when he attempted an expansive sweep and top-edged Parvez Sultan (3/94) to wicketkeeper Sentu Sarkar. But the youngster had done enough to ensure his team was in the driver’s seat.Speaking about the years between the call-ups Aneeshwar said, “I’ve waited a long time for this moment. It's been a hard grind and I've played three years of U-23 and led Karnataka for two years. I knew I would have to wait for my opportunity and score a lot of runs to come back into the team. When the runs weren't coming for a season, I knew hard work would get me back into the side. Once the runs started coming, my belief and confidence in my return increased.”SCOREBOARDTripura (I innings): 194.Karnataka (I innings; o/n 297/7): Aneeshwar Gautam c S Sarkar b Sultan 100, Manvanth Kumar lbw Sandip Sarkar 51, Ritesh Bhatkal (not out) 74, Shikhar Shetty (not out) 1. articles.title: South Africa vs Australia: Marnus Labuschagne hits record low but new guard stand up for tourists
articles.summary: Marnus Labuschagne's poor form hit a record low but Australia's new guard stood up to put the tourists in a strong position in the decisive Test against South Africa.
articles.body:
South Africa 329: Ackerman 95; Starc 6-72

Australia 330-4: Inglis 85*; Jansen 2-37

Marnus Labuschagne has been front and centre for an era of Australian cricket.

Chirping, chewing and, with bat in hand, often appearing to idolise and mimic his team-mate Steve Smith.

Smith has been ruled out of the enthralling decisive Test against South Africa with a neck injury.

Without him, Australia wanted their number three to feast at last chance saloon, where he has been perched for an eternity, on day two in Cape Town.

The 32-year-old lasted five deliveries and did not score a run.

Labuschagne failed to scored a Test century for the 48th time in a row - a new record for the number of consecutive innings a batter in Australia’s top four has waited to raise his bat at three figures.

"That will never be broken," said former Australia quick Jason Gillespie on ABC.

"I say that because, respectfully, I don't think anyone will be given that length of time again."

There was a time when, from his insertion into the 2019 Ashes as a concussion substitute until the end of England's next quest to win back the urn, Labuschagne averaged 65 in Test cricket.

Repeat that over a Test career and only Sir Donald Bradman's mark of 99.94 would be ahead.

Instead, since his last Test century at Old Trafford in 2023, he averages 24.77.

Labuschagne may get one more chance in this Test, should Australia not progress from their position of 330-4, leading by one run, and dismiss South Africa before needing to pad up again.

"I just feel it is too far gone now," Gillespie added. "It is a very big sample size. Australia are at a point where they need to look elsewhere."

Labuschagne's technique has been pored over again and again as his slump progressed.

In August, the great Ricky Ponting, one of his predecessors as Australia's number three, called for the axe to fall.

"He can't score off the back foot," was Ponting's cutting remark.

Having batted nicely in three or four innings in this series only to give it away after reaching 30, here he was stuck on the crease, playing back to a full ball and nicking spinner Simon Harmer to slip.

"That's nerves and the pressure the selectors have put him under for an extended period of time," said former Australia batter Simon Katich on SEN Radio.

"They put him in this position by not making the decision to give him a breather."

It felt like all of Labuschagne's issues collapsing into one.

But if his pained stare down the pitch signalled the end of something, what followed hinted at their future.

With Travis Head already out and Labuschagne following, the score 58-2 in reply to the Proteas' 329, there was no Smith to steer Australia out of this tricky spot.

Matt Renshaw, Cameron Green and Josh Inglis, three of the junior members of this side, instead made fifties and put their side in the ascendancy.

Renshaw is one of those who has been kept out by the selectors in the hope Labuschagne could rediscover his best form.

Had he been picked to open in the World Test Championship final against South Africa in 2025, rather than Australia's decision to try Labuschagne as opener, he may have spent the following 17 months ending the debate over who should replace David Warner.

Having got his chance in this series, initially as number five before the Nic Maddinson experiment was cut short after two Tests, the Middlesbrough-born Renshaw looks like being a fixture for this winter and beyond.

His 74 here, which followed a career-best 190 in Durban, suggests a return to England next summer awaits.

Green is one who has not lacked opportunity. Long viewed as Australia's golden boy, the 27-year-old has flicked across 39 previous Test without ever truly appearing comfortable.

In making 65 below Table Mountain, the towering all-rounder played with the composure and authority he has often lacked.

Most impressive, though, was Inglis - another Aussie who spent his early years in Yorkshire .

He had not faced the red ball since March, has had his preparations limited by a broken finger, and came in with South Africa buoyed by Marco Jansen dismissing Renshaw and Green in successive overs before tea.

The 31-year-old finished 85 not out in an unbroken partnership of 145 with Alex Carey. There would be no late-evening South Africa fightback, like the one Mitchell Starc inspired on day one to bowl South Africa out.

This is not to say everything has fallen into place for Australia. Smith will return, meaning Green and Inglis would likely move from their current batting positions of four and five for their next Test against New Zealand in December.

Smith has avoided batting in Labuschagne's position before, and a four-Test trial of Green in that spot in 2024 and 2025 was aborted after he returned 188 across eight innings.

Leeds-born Inglis, meanwhile, has three first-class matches worth experience at number three, in which he averaged 12.66 and has a best score of 29.

But if ever a day showed Australia there is merit in moving from one generation to another it was this.

Three of their less experienced players, albeit two of them have celebrated their 30th birthdays, stood up to take Australia to a position from which they can control this Test.

Labuschagne did not. His days look numbered.

articles.title: Molineux mania! UP Warriorz outgun RCB in Rs 1.10 cr showstopper at WPL auction
articles.summary: KOCHI: UP Warriorz, with the biggest purse of Rs 3.75 crore, beat Royal Challengers Bengaluru in a fierce bidding war to sign Australia captain Sophie
articles.body: KOCHI: UP Warriorz, with the biggest purse of Rs 3.75 crore, beat Royal Challengers Bengaluru in a fierce bidding war to sign Australia captain Sophie Molineux for Rs 1.10 crore at the WPL mini auction in Kochi on Wednesday.UP opened at Rs 50 lakh and RCB, for whom Molineux was part of the 2024 title-winning side, came straight back, and her price zoomed to Rs 95 lakh. UP then moved it to Rs 1 crore, the RCB countered at Rs 1.05 crore. UP finally pushed it to Rs 1.10 crore to seal the deal. Allrounder Molineux is the X-factor, who provides a wealth of experience for UP, and will be propped up as the perfect foil to her captain and compatriot, Meg Lanning.“We were determined to get Sophie at any cost,” UP Warriorz CEO Kshemal Waingankar told reporters. “It puts us in a good position with Sophie and Grace (Harris) combined to tweak our combinations and decide what works best for us.”UP added firepower to their batting by picking Australian Grace Harris for Rs 30 lakh, who returns to the franchise she represented in 2025. She had a prolific run in RCB’s 2026 title season, but was released with Ellyse Perry’s return. Harris is likely to open with Lanning or Pratika Rawal. With Harleen Deol also in the mix, it gives UP the legroom to mix and match their batters. “Grace brings power to the middle order, Molineux the leadership qualities,” Waingankar added.They also snapped up experienced Himachal wicketkeeper Sushma Verma and bid Rs 30 lakh for offspinner Sneh Rana. With Sophie Ecclestone and Deepti Sharma in the squad, their spin attack looks robust.Unlike previous seasons, UP went into this auction with a clear plan. “We carried out some experiments last season that didn’t work. This season, we were betting on experience, which is why we targeted players like Sushma Verma,” UP head coach Abhishek Nayar said.Combinations were the priority for the five franchises, and with the other four on limited purse, the bidding remained largely cautious.Gunalan Kamalini, the young India batter with a high ceiling went to Gujarat Giants who made the first bid at Rs 40 lakh. RCB opened their account by snapping up Australian left-arm spinner Jess Jonassen at a base price of Rs 40 lakh.Mumbai Indians (MI) pursued Kiran Navigare, a former UP player, for a base price of Rs 40 lakh. Delhi Capitals took the price to Rs 75 lakh, and MI, with only Rs 90 lakh left in their purse, dropped out.Sri Lankan veteran Chamari Athapaththu going unsold was the biggest surprise of the evening. MI played it smart by picking childhood friends Disha Kasat and Latika Imandar, two players from Vidarbha who have been making waves at the domestic level, for Rs 10 lakh each.The auction’s biggest takeaway was the continuing importance of domestic cricket to women’s game, with franchises backing a raft of players who have emerged from the circuit.Steal buysGrace Harris (Rs 30 lakh, UP): Apart from her blistering strokeplay, she can bowl offspin in the Powerplay.Sushma Verma (Rs 30 lakh, UP): An international player currently in stellar form. Got exposure in the CPL. She walks into UP’s playing XI given her keeping skills and experience.Disha Kasat (Rs 10 lakh, MI): An improved player from WPL 2023. She can be used as an opener.Kathryn Bryce (Rs 10 lakh, UP): Scotland captain, who can bowl medium pace and bat at the top of the order.Sanika Chalke (Rs 10 lakh, MI): Touted as the player of the future. Part of the 2025 U-19 T20 World Cup-winning squad.Samaira Raghav (Rs 10 lakh, GG): A16-year-old ex-sprinter who was pushed to cricket by her father. articles.title: Ireland Cricket: Skipper Paul Stirling out of remainder of Namibia series
articles.summary: Ireland captain Paul Stirling will miss the concluding two matches of his side's one-day international series in Namibia after fracturing his finger.
articles.body:
Ireland captain Paul Stirling will miss the final two games of his side's one-day international series in Namibia after fracturing his finger.

The 36-year-old sustained the injury while fielding during his side's loss in the third ODI on Tuesday, a result that leaves his side trailing their hosts 2-1 in the five-match series.

Tim Tector, brother of middle-order batter Harry Tector, has been called up as a replacement.

The younger Tector sibling is uncapped in ODIs, although he has made eight appearances for the side in T20 cricket, averaging 17 in the shorter format.

Battling to save the series, the injury to Stirling is another blow to head coach Gary Wilson.

The Ireland opener was unable to bat in his side's innings following the injury on Tuesday, but had a pair of half-centuries in the first two games in Windhoek, leading the side with scores of 56 and 77.

Ireland won the opener of the series on 22 October but have suffered losses of 31 and 63 runs in the two games since.

The series, which is being used by Ireland as preparation for next year's World Cup qualifiers, resumes on Friday before a concluding fixture on Sunday.

articles.body: The Women's Premier League (WPL) 2027 mini-auction in Kochi saw several prominent international cricketers and familiar domestic names fail to attract bids despite their experience and previous performances.With limited slots available across five franchises, teams had to prioritise their remaining budgets and specific squad requirements. The absence of bids for several established players highlighted the intense competition for places in the league.Chamari Athapaththu — Sri LankaSri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu was among the most notable names to go unsold. articles.title: Chicago Bears NFL Trade Deadline Targets
articles.summary: What’s the latest buzz with the Chicago Bears and the NFL trade deadline? @wiltfongjr examines it here.
articles.body:
The rumor mill ahead of the November 10 trade deadline has been churning for weeks, and the Chicago Bears have been front and center for much of it. Yesterday, the Indianapolis Colts made the biggest trade splashes so far, sending guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers, and reports were that the Bears checked on both players. While interest in Nelson was likely due diligence, their interest in Buckner was more serious because of their need on the defensive line.

In ESPN's latest trade deadline article from Jeremy Fowler (Insider) and Matt Bowen (Xs&Os), they speculate on several players who could be moved along with the best scheme fits. Here are who they see as logical for the Bears.

No player has more buzz to the Bears than Khalil Mack, but the winless Los Angeles Chargers seem content to stand pat. Fowler writes, "Returning to the Bears is a natural fit for the equivalent of a quality Day 3 pick."

The Arizona Cardinals' Josh Sweat (6'5″, 265) would give the Bears bookend Sweats up front. The 29-year-old had 12 sacks a season ago and 2 so far this season.

The Bears have been rumored to be in on defensive end Jermaine Johnson II (6'5″, 254) before, and with the Tennessee Titans in rebuild mode, they may be willing to move the 27-year-old.

The Titan who may make the most sense is cornerback Alontae Taylor, who has history with Chicago defensive coordinator Dennis Allen from their time in New Orleans. Taylor hasn't fit in with the Tennessee defense and has been a healthy scratch the last two games. His contract would require some work to fit in, but "He plays a premium position, and he has the speed to cover receivers on the perimeter or play a disruptive role in the slot," Bowen writes.

The article also lists other corners and d-linemen potentially on the trade block, which could lead to a very active deadline.

Looking around the league, several other teams could be sellers with defensive players the Bears could covet, including the Philadelphia Eagles, Washington Commanders, New Orleans Saints, Miami Dolphins, and New York Jets.

The Jets have a former Bear Pro Bowler who has yet to play a snap on defense for them, and could be had for a late pick or a pick swap. Cornerback Nahshon Wright seemingly wants to return to Chicago (just look at his Twitter profile pic), and while he was boom-or-bust in coverage in 2025, he'd fill a need for a secondary that's dealt with injuries all season.

From ESPN's Rich Cimini , who covers the Jets.

Nahshon Wright tells ESPN that he's "definitely frustrated" by having no role on defense. Asked if he has requested a trade, he said, "Not formally…(But) I've expressed my feelings (to the team)

Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer believes the Bears are in the defensive tackle market, and he mentions Washington's Daron Payne and Indianapolis' Grover Stewart as possibilities. He also drops Mack's name as a fit in Chicago.

Bears head coach Ben Johnson was asked today how involved he is with general manager Ryan Poles and their trade talks as the deadline looms.

"Well, yeah, there's a lot going on," Johnson said. "It's certainly Ryan's domain, and yet we have constant dialogue of what this team needs and where we can impact ourselves not just this year but, you know, years in the future as well. So he's turning over every stone that he possibly can to improve this football team, just like he has ever since I've gotten in this building, and I feel really good about our process, and we'll see what happens. Never know."

Do you expect any trade deadline additions?
